Check the inside length and width of the master link against the crane hook before ordering; the size tables give both dimensions and the WLL for each link.

categories.intro: Lifting slings are the flexible link between a crane hook and the load — chain, wire rope or synthetic — each rated for the way it is hitched. Indus supplies Grade 80 and Grade 100 chain slings with one to four legs, two-leg and ferrule-secured soft-eye wire rope slings, polyester round slings and flat webbing slings, a Grade 80 web sling connector and cable socks for pulling cable, from Dubai under IH-LR part numbers.

faq.q: Are cable socks for lifting?
faq.a: No. A cable sock is a pulling grip — it draws cable or hose through a duct or over rollers. Its breaking load is a pulling figure, and it is not rated for suspending a load.

faq.q: What is the difference between WLL, SWL and breaking load?
faq.a: WLL — working load limit — is the most the manufacturer rates a part to carry in service. SWL, safe working load, is the older term and is sometimes set lower for a particular installation. The minimum breaking load is what the part withstood in test, several times its WLL, and it is never a working figure.

faq.q: Do the parts come with test certificates?
faq.a: Yes. Each consignment ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. If your site needs more — third-party certification or witnessed proof testing — say so on the RFQ and we will confirm what we can arrange.

faq.q: Should I use a chain, wire rope or polyester sling?
faq.a: Use chain for hot, rough or abrasive loads and long service, wire rope for a strong, lighter sling on general steelwork, and polyester round or webbing slings where the load surface must not be marked. Chain tolerates sharp edges and heat best but is heavy. Wire rope is lighter per tonne but kinks and is damaged by crushing. Polyester is light and gentle on finished surfaces but must be protected from edges, heat and chemicals.

faq.q: How does a choke or basket hitch change what a sling can lift?
faq.a: A choke hitch lowers the rating and a basket hitch can raise it, by factors that depend on the sling type and the standard. For polyester slings to EN 1492, the choke factor is 0.8 and a basket with vertical legs is 2.0 times the straight-pull WLL. Chain and wire rope slings have their own factors, and an angled basket loses capacity like a two-leg sling. Read the factor for the hitch from the sling's own table.

faq.q: What do the colours of polyester slings mean?
faq.a: Under EN 1492-1 and EN 1492-2 the sling colour shows its working load limit in a straight pull: violet 1 t, green 2 t, yellow 3 t, grey 4 t, red 5 t, brown 6 t, blue 8 t and orange 10 t and above. The colour is a quick check only; the sewn-on label carries the rated WLL, material and traceability, and a sling with a missing or illegible label must come out of service.

categories.intro: Chain slings are lifting assemblies of alloy chain, a master link and end fittings, rated for the number of legs and the angle they work at. Indus supplies Grade 80 and Grade 100 chain slings in single-, two-, three- and four-leg make-ups with sling, grab, foundry or self-locking hooks or oblong links, made up to the reach you need, from Dubai.

faq.q: How do I read the make-up code?
faq.a: From the top down. The first letter is the number of legs: S single, D double, T triple, Q quad. The next is the top fitting, usually O for an oblong master link. The last is the bottom fitting: S sling hook, G grab hook, F foundry hook, SL self-locking hook, O oblong link. A DOS sling is a double-leg sling with a master link and sling hooks.

faq.q: What is the difference between WLL, SWL and breaking load?
faq.a: WLL — working load limit — is the most the manufacturer rates a part to carry in service. SWL, safe working load, is the older term and is sometimes set lower for a particular installation. The minimum breaking load is what the part withstood in test, several times its WLL, and it is never a working figure.

faq.q: How often must a chain sling be examined in the UAE?
faq.a: It depends on the rule your site works to. Abu Dhabi's Code of Practice 34 calls for a thorough examination of lifting accessories every 6 months by an approved third party. Dubai Municipality's guideline calls for certification at least every 12 months by an EIAC-accredited body. Either way the sling is checked by the user before each use.

faq.q: Do the slings come with test certificates?
faq.a: Yes. Each sling is tagged with its serial number, chain size, grade, reach and WLL and ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. If your site needs more — third-party certification or witnessed proof testing — say so on the RFQ and we will confirm what we can arrange.

faq.q: Why is a four-leg chain sling rated the same as a three-leg sling?
faq.a: Because on an uneven or rigid load only three of the four legs can be relied on to share the weight. EN 818-4 therefore gives three- and four-leg Grade 8 slings the same factor of 2.1 times a single leg for leg angles up to 45° from vertical. If the load's centre of gravity is off-centre or the legs are different lengths, two legs may carry almost all of it; then rate the sling as two-leg or worse.

faq.q: How is the reach of a chain sling measured?
faq.a: Reach is measured from the bearing point inside the master link to the bearing point of the bottom fitting, with the sling hanging straight. It is the effective working length, not the length of chain alone, and on a multi-leg sling every leg is made to the same reach unless you ask otherwise. When ordering, give the reach and check that the leg angle it produces on your load stays within the range the table rates.

categories.intro: Wire rope fittings are the clips, thimbles, ferrules, sleeves, sockets and terminals that form and protect an eye or end on steel wire rope. Indus supplies steel wire rope from 6x7 to 6x36WS, galvanized aircraft cable and stainless 1x7 and 1x19 strand, with DIN 741, DIN 1142, US and JIS clips, EN 13411-3 aluminium and stainless ferrules, oval and hourglass sleeves, BS 464, DIN 6899 and US-pattern thimbles, G-416 pattern spelter sockets and stainless swage terminals, from Dubai.

faq.q: How many wire rope clips does an eye need?
faq.a: It depends on the rope diameter and the clip type, and the clip maker's table is the authority. The U-bolt goes on the dead (short) end and the saddle on the live end — "never saddle a dead horse" — and the nuts are re-torqued after the first load.

faq.q: What is the difference between a fibre core and a steel core?
faq.a: A fibre core (FC) makes the rope more flexible; an independent wire rope core (IWRC) resists crushing on a drum and carries a higher breaking load for the same diameter. The size tables give both where the manufacturer publishes them.

faq.q: Do the parts come with test certificates?
faq.a: Yes. Each consignment ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. If your site needs more — third-party certification or witnessed proof testing — say so on the RFQ and we will confirm what we can arrange.

faq.q: Should I order ordinary lay or Lang's lay wire rope?
faq.a: Choose ordinary (regular) lay for general lifting and slings, and Lang's lay only where abrasion and bending fatigue dominate and both rope ends are fixed against rotation. In ordinary lay the wires run opposite to the strands, so the rope resists kinking and crushing and is easier to handle. In Lang's lay the wires and strands run the same way, giving more wearing surface but a rope that tends to untwist if one end is free, such as on a single-part hook block.

faq.q: How do I measure wire rope diameter?
faq.a: Measure across the outermost crowns of the strands, not across the flats, using a caliper with jaws wide enough to span at least two strands. Take two readings at right angles at each point and measure at two or more points along the rope, then use the average. New rope is usually slightly over its nominal size, and a reading below nominal on a used rope is a sign of wear or core damage.

faq.q: Which ferrule material should I use — aluminium, copper or stainless?
faq.a: Use the ferrule material the termination standard and the rope maker specify for that rope: aluminium ferrules to EN 13411-3 are the usual choice for galvanized and bright steel wire rope. Copper and stainless ferrules are used with stainless rope and in marine and corrosive service, where aluminium against stainless can corrode. Whatever the material, the ferrule must match the rope diameter and be pressed with the die made for it.

categories.intro: Wire rope thimbles are grooved steel inserts fitted inside a rope eye to keep its shape, spread the bearing load and stop the rope wearing or kinking where it meets a shackle, hook or pin. Indus supplies BS 464, DIN 6899 A and B, DIN 3091 solid, AS 1138, JIS, European and Italian pattern thimbles, G-411 standard and G-414 extra heavy pattern thimbles, tube thimbles with and without gusset, and fibre and synthetic rope thimbles, galvanized or stainless, from Dubai.

guidance.heading: Choosing a thimble
guidance.body: First decide the rope: wire rope thimbles have a narrow groove, while fibre and synthetic rope thimbles are made wider for the softer rope. Then the rope diameter, which the thimble must match exactly. Next the duty: a standard plate thimble for general eyes, an extra heavy pattern where a pin bears hard, and a solid or tube thimble where the eye is loaded on a pin and must not close up. Check the inside of the thimble clears the shackle pin or hook. Finally the finish, galvanized or stainless. To quote, send the rope type and diameter, the pin or hook size, the pattern or standard, material and quantity.

standards.heading: EN 13411-1 and the older patterns
standards.body: EN 13411-1 is the current European standard for thimbles in steel wire rope slings. It covers non-welded plate thimbles for six- and eight-strand ropes from 8 mm to 60 mm to EN 12385-4, and does not cover reeving or solid thimbles. It succeeded DIN 3090, which itself replaced DIN 6899; DIN 6899 is withdrawn but its A and B forms are still widely made. BS 464, DIN 3091 solid thimbles, AS 1138 and JIS thimbles, and the US G-411 and G-414 patterns are separate dimension series and do not map one to one.

faq.q: When do I need an extra heavy thimble?
faq.a: Where the eye is loaded through a shackle pin or hook that bears hard on it. An extra heavy thimble has a deeper groove and thicker body that resists being crushed or pulled out of shape.

faq.q: Do the parts come with test certificates?
faq.a: Yes. Each consignment ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. If your site needs more — third-party certification or witnessed proof testing — say so on the RFQ and we will confirm what we can arrange.

faq.q: How do I choose the right thimble size?
faq.a: Choose the thimble made for your rope's nominal diameter, then check its inside length and width clear the pin or hook it will sit on. A thimble too large lets the rope roll out of the groove under load, and one too small pinches the rope and cannot be closed properly by the ferrule or clips. Thimbles from different standards differ in groove and eye size for the same rope, so compare the size table dimensions.

faq.q: Can I use a wire rope thimble on synthetic or fibre rope?
faq.a: Not as a rule: fibre and synthetic rope need a thimble with a wider, rounder groove made for them. A wire rope thimble's narrow groove and edges cut into the softer rope and the rope can roll out. This shelf carries manila, fibre (K3) and synthetic rope thimbles for that purpose. For high-modulus ropes such as UHMWPE, follow the rope maker's minimum bend diameter at the eye.

faq.q: When should I use a solid or tube thimble instead of a plate thimble?
faq.a: Use a solid or tube thimble where the eye bears directly on a pin and heavy loading would squeeze a plate thimble closed. An open plate thimble can deform and let the rope bear on the pin, while a solid or tube thimble keeps the eye's bore round and spreads the load. Tube thimbles with a gusset add stiffness across the eye. Check the bore against the pin diameter in the size table.

faq.q: Are galvanized and stainless thimbles interchangeable?
faq.a: Match the thimble material to the rope and the environment rather than swapping freely. Use stainless thimbles on stainless rope and in marine or corrosive service, and galvanized thimbles on galvanized rope. Mixing stainless with galvanized or bright steel in salt water speeds corrosion of the less noble part, and the dimensions of stainless and galvanized patterns are not always identical, so check the table for the rope size.

categories.intro: Load securing and marine hardware covers the gear that holds a load or a vessel in place rather than lifting it: lashings, binders, rope, anchors, chain, bollards and fenders. Indus supplies ratchet straps in 2″, 3″ and 4″ widths, claw, ratchet, lever and Grade 100 load binders, PP, PE, nylon, polyester and UHMWPE rope and twine, delta, Bruce, Hall, Admiralty, stockless and plough anchors, anchor chain end shackles, marine and dock bollards, cleats and rubber and foam fenders, from Dubai.

guidance.heading: Securing a load or mooring a vessel
guidance.body: For transport, work out the securing force first, then choose the method: friction lashing relies on the tension the strap or binder puts in, direct lashing on the lashing capacity. Choose ratchet straps by LC and STF, and chain binders by the chain grade and size they are marked for. For rope, choose fibre by stretch, buoyancy and UV exposure. For mooring, size anchors, bollards and fenders to the vessel and berth design. To quote, send the application, the rated capacity or size, length, quantity and any standard or class certificate required.

standards.heading: EN 12195 and the rope standards
standards.body: EN 12195 covers load restraint on road vehicles: Part 1 the calculation of securing forces, Part 2 web lashings made from man-made fibres, Part 3 lashing chains and Part 4 steel wire rope lashings. Grade 70 transport chain and binders on this site are also offered to AS/NZS 4344, the Australian load-restraint standard. Fibre ropes are made to ISO product standards by fibre, such as ISO 1140 polyamide, ISO 1141 polyester, ISO 1346 polypropylene and ISO 1969 polyethylene, with properties tested to ISO 2307.

faq.q: Are load binders lifting equipment?
faq.a: No. A load binder tensions a chain tie-down to secure a load for transport. Its WLL is a tensioning rating and it is not for lifting.

faq.q: Do the parts come with test certificates?
faq.a: Yes. Each consignment ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. If your site needs more — third-party certification or witnessed proof testing — say so on the RFQ and we will confirm what we can arrange.

faq.q: What do LC and STF mean on a ratchet strap label?
faq.a: LC is the lashing capacity, the maximum force the strap may take in direct pull, and STF is the standard tension force, the tension the ratchet leaves in the strap after a standard hand force. Both are marked in daN under EN 12195-2. Direct lashing calculations use LC; friction or top-over lashing depends on STF, because the load is held by pressing it onto the deck. A strap with a high LC but low STF does little in a friction lashing.

faq.q: Which load binder fits my chain?
faq.a: Use a binder marked for your chain's size range and rated at least to the chain's working load limit. Load binders are made for a range of chain sizes, often marked on the handle, and the hooks must seat on the chain links without being forced. Match the grade too: a Grade 70 binder on Grade 70 transport chain, and the Grade 100 binder where the lashing uses Grade 100 chain. The lowest-rated part sets the lashing's capacity.

faq.q: Which fibre ropes float?
faq.a: Polypropylene and polyethylene ropes float; nylon (polyamide) and polyester ropes sink. Floating rope is used for rescue lines, buoy lines and mooring lines that should stay clear of propellers. Polypropylene is light and cheap but loses strength in strong sunlight faster than polyester or nylon. Where shock loads matter, nylon's stretch absorbs energy; where low stretch matters, polyester or UHMWPE is the better choice.

faq.q: What is a high holding power (HHP) anchor?
faq.a: An HHP anchor is one whose holding power has been proven by tests to be higher than an ordinary stockless anchor of the same mass. Under classification society rules, an approved HHP anchor may weigh up to 25% less than the stockless anchor the vessel's equipment number calls for. The reduction applies only to an anchor type approved as HHP by the vessel's class society, so ask for the type approval with the order.

categories.intro: Bollards are short, heavy posts on a ship's deck or a quay that mooring and towing lines are made fast to. Indus supplies marine double and cross bollards to GB/T 554, ISO 13795, JIS F 2001, DIN 82607, NS 2584 and CB/T standards, single bitt, twin horn, stag horn, curved and inclined bollards, T, J, K, R-head and CVI dock bollards, and stainless cleats, chocks, fairleads and bow rollers, from Dubai.

standards.heading: Bollard standards
standards.body: Ship bollards are built to standards that fix their types, nominal sizes and principal dimensions, so a bollard is ordered by standard, type and nominal size. ISO 13795 covers welded steel bollards for sea-going vessels, including materials, construction and marking. GB/T 554 is the Chinese national standard, JIS F 2001 the Japanese and DIN 82607 the German; the same nominal size does not give the same dimensions or rating across them. The load figures in each size table are as published for that standard and edition.

faq.q: What does the nominal size of a marine bollard mean?
faq.a: For a double bollard to GB/T 554, ISO 13795 or JIS F 2001, the nominal size is the diameter of the pillar in millimetres; the standard sets the safe working load and dimensions that go with it. Quote the standard, the type and the nominal size on the RFQ.

faq.q: Should I fit a double bollard or a cross bollard?
faq.a: Fit a double bollard where lines are made fast in figure-of-eight turns around two posts, and a cross bollard where a single post with a cross bar or horns must stop the turns riding up. Double bollards suit larger vessels and heavy mooring lines. Cross bollards are common on smaller craft and where the line leads up at an angle. Either way, match the type and nominal size to the vessel's mooring arrangement drawing.

faq.q: Can I replace a JIS bollard with a GB/T 554 or ISO 13795 bollard of the same nominal size?
faq.a: Not without checking, because each standard sets its own pillar spacing, base dimensions, plate thickness and load for a given nominal size. A replacement must fit the existing deck reinforcement and carry the load the mooring arrangement was designed for. Compare the drawings and size tables side by side, and on a classed vessel confirm the change with the class surveyor before ordering.

faq.q: How is a dock bollard fixed to a quay?
faq.a: A dock bollard is held down by anchor bolts cast into the quay concrete, usually with an anchor plate or frame below, and the base is grouted level. The number, size and embedment of the bolts are part of the bollard's design and must be checked by the quay's structural engineer for the line pull. Order the anchor bolt set with the bollard so the pattern matches, and set it to template before the concrete is poured.

faq.q: What is the difference between a bollard, a fairlead and a chock?
faq.a: A bollard is the strongpoint the line is made fast to; a fairlead or chock only guides the line to it and keeps it from chafing on the deck edge. Fairleads and chocks change the line's direction and so carry load, but the line is not belayed on them. Their position and size come from the same mooring arrangement as the bollards, and the line diameter decides the opening needed.

faq.q: What do I need to send for a bollard quotation?
faq.a: Send the standard, type and nominal size for each bollard, the material, the quantity, and whether it is for a ship's deck or a quay. Add the vessel's class society if a class certificate is needed, and for dock bollards whether you need the anchor bolt set. If you only have an old bollard to replace, send its dimensions and any markings, and we will match it to a standard or say where it does not fit one.

faq.q: Which tube do these fit?
faq.a: Fractional-inch outside-diameter tube from 1/16" to 2", plus metric tube on the metric connectors. Choose the wall thickness from the pressure table on each listing.

faq.q: Do you list equivalent part numbers?
faq.a: Where the manufacturer cross-references a Swagelok part number, the size table shows it beside the Indus part number.

faq.q: Can I use Indus tube fittings with Swagelok, Parker A-LOK or CPI nuts and ferrules?
faq.a: No. Compression fittings from different makers should not be intermixed, even where the design and size look the same. Ferrule geometry, body cone angles, thread tolerances and hardening differ from maker to maker, and a joint assembled from mixed parts may not grip or seal as either maker designed it. Keep the body, nut and ferrules of each joint from the Indus range. A cross-referenced part number on a size table tells you which Indus part does the same job; it does not make the parts interchangeable.

faq.q: NPT, BSPP or SAE straight thread: which end connection do I need on a tube fitting?
faq.a: The one the port you are connecting to already has. NPT is a tapered thread that seals on the thread itself with a thread sealant or PTFE tape. BSPP and SAE straight threads are parallel and do not seal on the thread: BSPP seals with a bonded seal or metal gasket at the face, and SAE straight thread seals with an O-ring against the port. Fitting a tapered male into a parallel port, or the reverse, will not seal reliably. If you are unsure, send a photo of the port or measure the thread pitch and diameter.

faq.q: What tubing should be used with 316 stainless compression fittings?
faq.a: Seamless or welded-and-drawn 316 stainless tube, fully annealed, with a hardness below that of the fitting so the ferrules can bite into it. Instrument tubing to ASTM A269 or A213 is the usual specification. The outside diameter must be within tolerance and the surface free of scratches, weld beads or flats where the ferrule seats, since the seal forms on the tube surface. Cut the tube square, deburr it and bottom it fully in the fitting body before tightening. Choose the wall thickness from the pressure table on each listing.

faq.q: Is 316 stainless enough for offshore and coastal instrument lines in the Gulf?
faq.a: For many installations yes, but not for all. 316 resists general corrosion well, but warm, chloride-laden air and salt deposits can cause pitting and crevice corrosion, typically under clamps and at the tube-to-fitting crevice. Where a project specification calls for a higher alloy such as 6Mo super-austenitic or super duplex stainless for these conditions, the fittings must match that specification; this range is 316 only. Keeping tubing clean and properly supported and avoiding trapped moisture under clamps reduces the risk on 316 lines.

faq.q: Can I buy ferrules separately?
faq.a: Yes: front ferrules, back ferrules, ferrule sets and nuts are listed as their own parts.

faq.q: How many turns do I tighten a double-ferrule fitting from finger-tight?
faq.a: Follow the make-up instruction for the Indus fitting; for this design it is typically 1-1/4 turns past finger-tight for 1/4″ to 1″ tube and 3/4 turn for 1/16″ to 3/16″ tube. Insert the tube until it bottoms in the body, run the nut up finger-tight, mark the nut at the six o'clock position, then hold the body steady and turn the nut the specified amount. Counting turns from a mark is more reliable than tightening to a torque. Larger sizes may need a different procedure or a preset tool, so check the listing before making up tube above 1″.

faq.q: What is a gap inspection gauge used for on double-ferrule fittings?
faq.a: It checks that a fitting has been tightened enough on its first make-up. After pull-up, the gauge is offered into the gap between the nut and the body hex: if it will not enter, the fitting has been turned far enough; if it slips in, the fitting is under-tightened and needs more turn. It is a check for the initial make-up only. A fitting that has been disconnected and remade sits closer to the body, so the gauge does not apply to remakes.

faq.q: Can a double-ferrule fitting be taken apart and made up again?
faq.a: Yes. Once made up, the ferrules stay on the tube, so the joint can be disconnected and remade. To remake, put the tube and preswaged ferrules back into the body, run the nut up by hand to its previous position, then tighten slightly with a wrench until it is firm; do not repeat the full first make-up turns. Replace the nut and ferrules, and cut back the tube, if the ferrules or tube end are damaged or the joint will not seal.

faq.q: What is a positionable elbow or tee with an SAE straight thread?
faq.a: A fitting that can be turned to face any direction before it is locked, so the tube outlet lines up without forcing the tube. The male end has an SAE straight thread with a locknut, a backup washer and an O-ring. Screw it into the port until the washer meets the port face, back it off to the direction you need, up to one full turn, then hold the body and tighten the locknut. The O-ring, not the thread, makes the seal, so check that the port is an SAE straight-thread O-ring port before fitting it.

faq.q: What are the O-seal connectors marked vacuum for?
faq.a: They connect tube to a threaded port where a thread-sealed joint is not tight enough, such as vacuum and low-pressure gas lines. The male end carries an O-ring that seals against the port, so the joint does not depend on tape or sealant in the threads, which can leak or outgas under vacuum. Choose the O-ring material for the medium and temperature, and check the pressure rating on the listing, which may be lower than that of the standard male connector.

faq.q: Do you have metric single-ferrule connectors?
faq.a: Yes: the metric male connector covers metric tube from 2 mm to 38 mm to BSPT male threads.

faq.q: Will a 1/4″ tube fitting work on 6 mm tube, or 1/2″ on 12 mm?
faq.a: No. Fractional and metric tube sizes are close but not the same: 1/4″ is 6.35 mm against 6 mm, 3/8″ is 9.53 mm against 10 mm, and 1/2″ is 12.7 mm against 12 mm. A ferrule made for one will not grip or seal the other properly, and the joint can leak or blow off under pressure. Measure the tube outside diameter before ordering, keep metric and fractional fittings apart in stores, and order the metric connector for metric tube.

faq.q: What is a bored-through thermocouple connector?
faq.a: A male connector bored right through to the tube size, so a thermocouple sheath, probe or tube can pass through the fitting and out the other side. The ferrule grips and seals on the probe, which lets you set the insertion depth into a vessel or pipe where you want it, with the NPT male end screwed into the process port. Order it by the probe outside diameter, not the nominal thermocouple size, and remember that once the ferrule is made up its position on the probe is fixed.

faq.q: Where is a bulkhead fitting used, and what is a welding bulkhead union?
faq.a: A bulkhead fitting carries a tube line through a panel, enclosure wall or plate and holds it there. The standard type passes through a drilled hole and is clamped by a locknut on the far side, so it can be removed. A welding bulkhead union has no locknut: its body is welded into the plate, for a permanent, sealed pass-through. Check the panel thickness against the bulkhead length on the listing, and the hole size the fitting needs.

faq.q: What is a port connector?
faq.a: A short connector that joins two tube fitting ends directly, without a length of tube between them. Each end goes into a fitting port where the tube would normally go and is made up with that fitting's nut and ferrule, so two fittings, or a fitting and a valve, can be coupled as close as possible. A reducing port connector does the same between two different tube sizes. Like any part of the joint, use it only with fittings of the same system.

faq.q: What is a tube stub adapter or reducer used for?
faq.a: It has a tube-shaped end, the stub, in place of a nut and ferrule, and that stub plugs into another fitting's tube port as if it were tube. A reducer, tube × tube stub, changes the line from one tube size to another at an existing fitting. An adapter, tube stub × BSPP or NPT, turns a tube port into a threaded connection. They save a separate union and short tube piece where space is tight. Make up the stub in the mating fitting the same way as tube.

categories.intro: Metallic hose is corrugated metal tubing, usually stainless steel or a nickel alloy, with a wire braid that carries the pressure, used where heat, cold, fire, gas permeation or aggressive chemicals rule out rubber and plastic hose. On this page Indus supplies from Dubai annular and helical stainless hose, Inconel 625, Hastelloy C276, Monel 400 and bronze hose, high-pressure, cryogenic, oxygen, chlorine, steam-jacketed and heated assemblies, fire jackets, hose guards and couplings, from Thorburn Flex, Senior Flexonics, Hose Master, Witzenmann and Dixon.

faq.q: Why do metal hoses fail early?
faq.a: Usually from torsion, or from flexing in more than one plane. Install a metal hose without twist, flex it in a single plane and keep it within its minimum bend radius. A hose twisted during installation, or asked to absorb movement in two directions, fatigues far faster than its pressure rating suggests.

faq.q: Do you supply PTFE hose as well?
faq.a: Yes — smoothbore and convoluted PTFE hose with stainless or polypropylene braid, for chemical transfer and high temperatures where a metal hose is not needed.

faq.q: What end connections are available?
faq.a: Flanges, threaded ends and couplings fitted to suit the line, including ANSI Class 150 flanged assemblies. Tell us the mating connection and we will confirm the build.

faq.q: Does a metal hose keep its pressure rating at high temperature?
faq.a: No. Published working pressures for metal hose are given at room temperature and fall as the temperature rises, because the strength of the braid, the corrugated tube and the end attachment all drop with heat. Each maker publishes temperature correction factors for its alloys and for how the ends are attached, welded, brazed or crimped. Multiply the rated pressure by the factor for your operating temperature and check the result still exceeds the line pressure, including surges. Send us the medium, pressure and temperature and we size the hose to them.

faq.q: What is the difference between static and dynamic bend radius on a metal hose?
faq.a: The static bend radius is the tightest bend for a hose that is bent once at installation and then stays put; the dynamic bend radius is the larger radius allowed for a hose that flexes repeatedly in service. Bending tighter than the dynamic radius on a moving hose concentrates strain in the corrugations and shortens its life sharply. Both figures depend on the bore, corrugation profile and braid, so take them from the listing for the hose you choose.

faq.q: Can a braided metal hose absorb axial expansion in a pipe run?
faq.a: Not directly. The braid locks the hose length, so a braided hose installed in line with the pipe cannot stretch or compress to take up thermal growth; it can only absorb movement at right angles to its axis or angular movement. To take axial expansion, install the hose in an offset or a loop, so pipe movement becomes a bend in the hose, or use an expansion joint. Pipe loops built for this purpose are on this shelf.

categories.intro: Storz couplings are symmetrical quick-connect hose couplings, in which two identical heads lock together with a twist, used on fire-service, dewatering and water-transfer hose. On this page Indus supplies Sunpool Storz couplings and adapters from Dubai: long-shank hose couplings, male and female thread adapters, swivel female adapters, couplings with safety latches, reducers, UL-listed fire department connections and 30° elbows, gaskets and clamps, in aluminium, brass and stainless steel, from 25 to 150 mm.

faq.q: Do Storz couplings need a gasket?
faq.a: Yes — the seal is a gasket in each head, and suction service uses a different gasket from pressure service. Both are on this shelf. Replace a hardened or cracked gasket rather than forcing the heads tighter.

faq.q: Can two different Storz sizes connect?
faq.a: Not directly. A head connects only to a head of the same size; a reducer joins two sizes.

faq.q: What is an FDC?
faq.a: A fire department connection — the inlet on a building’s fire-protection system where fire service hose connects. The Storz FDCs here are UL listed.

faq.q: What does a Storz size such as 52-C or 75-B mean, and will they connect?
faq.a: The number is the nominal hose bore in millimetres and the letter is the head size, set by the distance between the lugs: D is 31 mm, C is 66 mm, B is 89 mm and A is 133 mm. Heads connect only when their lug distance matches, so a 52-C and a 42-C, which share the C head, couple to each other, while a C head will not couple to a B. North American Storz is usually named in inches, so measure the lug distance or send a photo with a rule across the head when matching a coupling already in service.

faq.q: Aluminium, brass or stainless steel Storz couplings: which should I choose?
faq.a: Aluminium for portable fire and dewatering hose, where weight matters and the water is clean; hard-anodised aluminium adds wear and corrosion resistance. Brass for heavier-duty and longer-life service and for water with some salt or contamination. Stainless steel for seawater, chemicals, food and process plant, where corrosion resistance and cleanability count. Heads of the same size connect whatever the material, but for permanent connections avoid leaving dissimilar metals coupled in wet, salty conditions.

faq.q: What does the safety latch on a Storz coupling do?
faq.a: It locks the two heads once they are turned together, so vibration, hose movement or a knock cannot rotate them apart. A standard Storz joint is held only by friction between the lugs and the gasket compression, and a hose that whips or is dragged can work it loose. The latch has to be released by hand before the heads can be turned to uncouple. It suits pressurised fire lines, fixed connections and any service where an accidental disconnection would be dangerous.

categories.intro: Cam and groove couplings, also called camlocks, are quick-connect couplings in which a grooved male adapter is locked into a female coupler by two cam arms, used on hose, pipe and tank connections for low-to-medium-pressure liquid and dry-bulk transfer. On this page Indus supplies Sealfast cam and groove couplings from Dubai in Types A to F, DA, DD, dust caps and plugs, with standard, self-locking and CrimpTEK crimp-shank versions and 45° and 90° elbows.

faq.q: Are cam and groove couplings suitable for high pressure?
faq.a: They are built for low-to-medium-pressure transfer, and the rating falls as the size rises. Check the working pressure of the size and material you need against the line; for high-pressure hydraulics use threaded or flanged connections instead.

faq.q: What does self-locking add?
faq.a: Cam arms that lock closed, so vibration or a snagged handle cannot open them. They suit transfer lines that are dragged or vibrate, and anywhere an uncoupling would spill.

faq.q: What is CrimpTEK?
faq.a: A cam and groove coupling with a crimp shank in place of a barbed hose shank. It is crimped onto the hose for retention instead of being clamped.

faq.q: Is a 2″ cam and groove coupling sized by the hose bore or the thread?
faq.a: Both: the nominal size is the same across the coupling. A 2″ Type C or E fits 2″ inside-diameter hose, a 2″ Type A, B, D or F has a 2″ NPT thread, and all 2″ couplers and adapters mate with each other. Size from the hose bore or the pipe size, not from the outside diameter of the coupling head. Reducing combinations need a reducing part or an adapter, because a 2″ adapter will not lock into a 3″ coupler.

faq.q: Which half of a cam and groove coupling holds the gasket, and which gasket material do I need?
faq.a: The gasket sits in the female coupler, Types B, C, D, DC and DD, and seals against the end of the male adapter. Buna-N (nitrile) is the usual choice for petroleum oils and fuels; EPDM for water, hot water, steam condensate and many acids and alkalis but not for oils; Viton (FKM) for aromatic fuels, many solvents and higher temperatures; and PTFE or PTFE-encapsulated gaskets for the widest chemical resistance. Check the gasket against the medium and temperature, and replace it when it is cut, flattened or swollen.

faq.q: What are Type DA and Type DD cam and groove couplings for?
faq.a: They join two coupling ends without a hose or thread in between. A Type DA has a female coupler on one end and a male adapter on the other, so it can extend a connection or turn its direction as an elbow. A Type DD has a female coupler on both ends and connects two male adapters, for example two hose ends fitted with Type E. Both are offered here in elbow forms to change the direction of a line at the connection.

categories.intro: Molykote greases are specialty lubricating greases, a base oil held in a thickener and often fortified with solids such as MoS₂ or PTFE, used where general-purpose grease fails on temperature, load, chemicals, plastics or food contact. Indus supplies them from Dubai: silicone greases 33, 41, 44 and 55, PFPE greases HP-300 and HP-500, MoS₂ bearing greases BR-2 Plus and Longterm 2 Plus, FM food-machinery greases such as G-4500 and G-0060, plastic-part greases EM-30L and PG-65, 3452 valve grease and DC HVG vacuum grease.

guidance.heading: Pick the grease by temperature, load and what it touches
guidance.body: Fix the operating temperature range first, since it rules out whole base-oil families. Then the duty: speed and load, with shock or slow, heavily loaded movement calling for an EP or MoS₂ grease. Then compatibility with every plastic, elastomer and process chemical the grease will touch, and food contact needing NSF H1. Last, consistency: the NLGI grade that suits the application method, softer for central lubrication systems and cold starts. Send the application, temperatures, speed and load, the product used now and the pack size.

standards.heading: NLGI grade, cone penetration and dropping point
standards.body: The NLGI consistency grade is set by worked cone penetration measured to ASTM D217, in tenths of a millimetre: NLGI 1 is 310–340, NLGI 2 is 265–295 and NLGI 3 is 220–250, so a lower grade is softer. Dropping point, to ASTM D2265, is the temperature at which the grease drips from a test cup; it is not a service temperature, and the maker's published service range on each data sheet is the figure to design to. FM grades for incidental food contact are registered by NSF as H1, grade by grade.

faq.q: What is the difference between Molykote 33 Light and 33 Medium, or 44 Light and 44 Medium?
faq.a: Light and Medium are the same silicone grease made to two consistencies: Light is softer, Medium stiffer. The softer version feeds more easily, suits lightly loaded and low-temperature mechanisms and small instrument bearings, and is easier to apply through grease lines; the stiffer version stays in place better in larger bearings and on vertical or open surfaces. Base oil and chemistry are the same, so choose by how the grease is applied and retained. Check the NLGI grade and temperature range on the data sheet of each.

faq.q: Which Molykote grease should I use on plastic gears and plastic-on-metal parts?
faq.a: Use a grease made for plastics, such as Molykote EM-30L, EM-50L, EM-D110 or PG-65 Plastislip, rather than a general mineral-oil grease. Some base oils and additives can soften, swell or stress-crack plastics such as polycarbonate and ABS, and the plastic grades are formulated to avoid that while damping noise and reducing wear in small gearboxes, slides and switches. Compatibility still depends on the exact polymer and the stress in the part, so test on the actual component before committing a production line.

faq.q: Which Molykote grease is for heavily loaded, slow-moving or shock-loaded bearings?
faq.a: An extreme-pressure grease with molybdenum disulphide, such as Molykote BR-2 Plus or Longterm 2 Plus. Both are lithium-soap greases with MoS₂, made for metal-on-metal rolling and plain bearings that run slowly to moderately fast under high load, vibration or shock, where an ordinary grease film would be squeezed out. They are not the choice for very high speed or extreme temperatures; for those, look at a synthetic or PFPE grade and check its speed factor on the data sheet.

faq.q: Which grease for a valve exposed to fuel, solvents or aggressive chemicals?
faq.a: Molykote 3452 Chemical Resistant Valve Grease. It is a fluorosilicone oil thickened with PTFE, made to stay in place on valve plugs, seats, stems and seals where fuels, solvents and many chemicals would wash out or dissolve a mineral or plain silicone grease. For the most aggressive media and highest temperatures, a PFPE grease such as HP-300 or HP-500 goes further. Send the medium, its concentration and the temperature so the grade can be confirmed against the data sheet.

faq.q: Can I mix two greases, or switch a bearing to a different Molykote grease?
faq.a: Do not mix them without confirming they are compatible. Greases with different thickeners, lithium, calcium, polyurea, PTFE or clay, or with different base oils such as mineral, silicone and PFPE, can soften, harden or bleed oil when mixed, and the bearing may then run dry. When changing grease, clean out the old grease where you can, or purge it with the new grease until only the new product emerges, and shorten the relubrication interval for the first few cycles. The data sheets give thickener and base oil for each grade.

faq.q: What is dielectric grease or vacuum grease used for, and is silicone grease safe near paint lines?
faq.a: Dielectric grease such as Molykote G-5008 is a non-conductive silicone that seals electrical connectors, boots and terminals against moisture and corrosion; DC HVG high vacuum grease seals and lubricates vacuum joints, stopcocks and O-rings. Both are silicone, and silicone residue on parts that will be painted, coated or bonded causes adhesion failures and surface defects such as fish-eyes, so keep them away from paint shops and bonding areas or use a non-silicone grease there.

categories.intro: Molykote oils and fluids are synthetic and silicone lubricating oils for gearboxes, compressors, vacuum pumps, chains, mechanical seals and viscous drives where a mineral oil would oxidise, thin out or contaminate the product. Indus supplies them from Dubai: Molykote 211 silicone fluid from 2,000 to 30,000 cSt, L-series synthetic gear oils in ISO VG 150, 220 and 460, compressor, process gas and vacuum pump oils, L-1605FM barrier fluid, and CO-220 and L-1468FM chain oils, many as FM food-machinery grades.

guidance.heading: Match the oil to the machine, then the viscosity
guidance.body: Start with the machine type, because gear, compressor, vacuum pump, chain and seal oils are formulated differently and are not interchangeable. For compressors, also state the gas compressed: air, or a hydrocarbon or reactive process gas. Then take the viscosity grade from the equipment maker's manual, and confirm temperature range, food-contact needs (NSF H1 FM grades) and compatibility with the oil already in the system and its seals. Send the machine make and model, the oil in use now, the operating temperatures and the volume needed.

standards.heading: ISO viscosity grades and silicone fluid viscosity
standards.body: Industrial oils are graded by ISO 3448: the ISO VG number is the mid-point kinematic viscosity in cSt at 40°C, and an oil must fall within ±10% of it, so ISO VG 220 covers 198 to 242 cSt. Silicone fluids such as Molykote 211 are sold by their viscosity in cSt measured at 25°C, which is a different reference temperature and not an ISO grade. FM grades for incidental food contact are registered by NSF as H1, grade by grade; check the registration on the data sheet of the exact product.

faq.q: What does ISO 150, 220 or 460 mean on a Molykote gear oil?
faq.a: It is the ISO viscosity grade: the oil's kinematic viscosity at 40°C in centistokes, within ±10%. Molykote L-1115FM is ISO VG 150, L-1122FM ISO VG 220 and L-1146FM ISO VG 460. Higher grades give a thicker film for slow, heavily loaded gears such as worm drives and large reducers; lower grades suit faster, lighter gears and cold starts. Use the grade the gearbox maker specifies, adjusted for ambient temperature if the manual allows, rather than moving between grades to cure a noise or temperature problem.

faq.q: What is Molykote 211 fluid and how do I choose its viscosity?
faq.a: Molykote 211 is a heat-stabilised dimethyl polysiloxane (silicone) fluid developed for viscous fan clutches, sold by viscosity in cSt at 25°C, from 2,000 to 30,000 cSt. In a viscous drive the fluid's shear resistance transmits torque, so the viscosity sets how strongly the clutch engages: replace it with the same cSt grade the unit was built with, from its service data. A different grade changes the engagement speed and the heat generated; mixing grades gives an intermediate viscosity that may not match either.

faq.q: What is a barrier fluid, and where is Molykote L-1605FM used?
faq.a: A barrier fluid fills the space between the two seals of a pressurised dual mechanical seal, held above process pressure so that any leakage across the inner seal is barrier fluid into the product rather than product to atmosphere. It must lubricate and cool the seal faces and be compatible with the process, since a little of it ends up there. L-1605FM is a synthetic barrier fluid registered for incidental food contact, which suits pumps and mixers in food, beverage and pharmaceutical plants. Confirm viscosity against the seal maker's recommendation.

faq.q: When does a compressor need a process gas oil instead of a standard compressor oil?
faq.a: When it compresses a hydrocarbon or reactive gas rather than air. Gases such as natural gas, propane or other process streams dissolve into many oils, thinning them and reducing film strength, and some react with or are contaminated by mineral oil. Process gas oils such as Molykote L-0268, L-1510 and L-1568 are formulated to resist that dilution. Send the gas composition, discharge pressure and temperature and the compressor type, because the right oil depends on all three.

faq.q: Can I switch a compressor or gearbox from mineral oil to a synthetic Molykote oil?
faq.a: Usually, but drain and flush rather than topping up. Some synthetic bases, polyalkylene glycols in particular, do not mix with mineral oil and can form deposits or separate; others mix but lose part of their benefit when diluted. Check seal and paint compatibility, drain the old oil hot, flush if the maker recommends it, refill and check the oil and filters after the first hours of running. Tell us the oil in use now and we confirm the changeover procedure for the grade you choose.

faq.q: Which chain oil for ovens, freezers or general conveyors?
faq.a: Choose by the chain's temperature. Molykote CO-220 is a multi-purpose chain oil for general conveyor and drive chains; L-1468FM is a synthetic freezer chain oil that stays fluid at freezer temperatures and is registered for incidental food contact, for chains in cold stores and spiral freezers. For hot chains in ovens and dryers, choose an oil whose published upper temperature covers the chain, so it does not leave carbon deposits. Apply to the pins and bushes, not just the outside of the plates.

categories.intro: Butterfly valves are quarter-turn valves in which a disc on a central stem rotates against a seat to open, throttle or shut a pipeline, used in water, HVAC, process, food and bulk-handling lines where a compact, light valve between flanges is wanted. Indus supplies DEMCO resilient-seated butterfly valves from Dubai: NE-C long-neck, NE-I short-neck and sanitary, NE-D lightweight-flange, NEI-T PTFE-lined and NF-C 14″–36″ series, wafer or lug, 200 psi, with DR pneumatic actuators, worm-gear operators and handles, plus Victaulic grooved Series 700 and Series 761.

guidance.heading: Series and body first, then trim, then operator
guidance.body: Choose the series by the line: NE-C long neck clears flange insulation, NE-I short neck for general and sanitary service, NE-D notched for lightweight flanges, NF-C for 14″ to 36″, NEI-T where the medium must touch only PTFE, Victaulic for grooved pipe. Then wafer or lug, then trim: body, disc and seat by medium and temperature. Then operator: handle to 12″, worm gear for larger or high-torque valves, pneumatic actuator for remote or automatic duty. Send size, medium, temperature, pressure, flange or groove standard and operator.

standards.heading: ASME Class 150 flanges and the valve's own rating
standards.body: DEMCO NE valves centre between ASME Class 125/150 flanges, and lug bodies are tapped for the Class 150 bolt pattern. The flange class does not set the valve's rating: the NE valves on this page are rated 200 psi shut-off, below the 285 psi a carbon steel Class 150 flange carries at ambient temperature, so the valve rating governs. Victaulic valves join roll- or cut-grooved pipe with Victaulic couplings, rated per valve: 200 psi for Series 700 and 300 psi for Series 761 as listed. The NE-I sanitary series uses FDA-compliant materials.

faq.q: What is the difference between DEMCO NE-C, NE-I, NE-D and NF-C butterfly valves?
faq.a: Mainly the neck and the size range. NE-C has a long neck, so the operator sits clear of up to 2″ of pipe insulation on Class 150 flanges, and is cast in wafer and tapped-lug patterns; NF-C is the large-bore long-neck series for 14″ to 36″. NE-I has a short neck for 2″ to 12″ valves between Class 125/150 flanges, in a wide choice of body materials, and is the basis of the sanitary versions. NE-D is short-necked with notches in the body to fit common lightweight flange patterns used in bulk handling and transport.

faq.q: How do I read a DEMCO butterfly part number such as J022122-1215311?
faq.a: The base number gives series and size: for 200 psi NE-C valves the last two digits run 19 for 2″ to 27 for 12″, so 22 is 4″. In the suffix, the first digit is body pattern (1 wafer, 5 lug), the second the body (1 ductile iron, 2 cast iron, 4 carbon steel), the third the stem (1 416 SS, 2 316 SS), the fourth the disc (2 316 SS, 3 Monel, 4 aluminium bronze, 5 nickel-plated ductile iron), then two digits for the seat (31 Buna-N, 34 Viton, 35 EPDM) and an operator code. Where the nameplate text and the code disagree, go by the nameplate.

faq.q: Which disc material should a DEMCO butterfly valve have?
faq.a: Choose the disc by what the medium does to metal, as you choose the seat by what it does to rubber. Nickel-plated ductile iron is the economical disc for water, air and other non-corrosive service; aluminium bronze suits seawater and brackish water; 316 stainless steel suits food, beverage, many chemicals and corrosive water; Monel is used for seawater and some acids and chlorides where stainless pits. Tell us the medium, concentration and temperature and we confirm disc, seat and stem together.

faq.q: Double-acting or spring-return pneumatic actuator for a butterfly valve?
faq.a: Spring-return if the valve must go to a safe position when air or power is lost; double-acting if it should stay where it was. A DEMCO DR spring-return actuator drives open with air and closes on its springs, or the reverse, so it fails closed or open as specified; a double-acting actuator uses air to drive both ways, is smaller for the same torque and holds its last position on air failure. Size either for the valve's seating torque at the available air supply pressure, and add a solenoid valve, limit switches or positioner as the control system needs.

faq.q: Do DEMCO butterfly valves need flange gaskets, and how should they be installed?
faq.a: No separate flange gaskets are normally needed: the resilient seat extends over the body faces and seals against the flanges. Install the valve with the disc slightly open so the seat is not pinched, centre it, then tighten the flange bolts evenly in a cross pattern. Check that the disc clears the bore of the adjoining pipe, fittings and any lined or heavy-wall pipe as it swings open. Never weld flanges with the valve between them, and fully cycle the valve before pressurising.

faq.q: When should I choose a Victaulic grooved butterfly valve instead of a flanged one?
faq.a: When the line is grooved pipe, typically in fire protection, HVAC, water and mining service. A grooved valve such as Victaulic Series 700 joins the pipe with two couplings, so there are no flange bolts to tighten, it installs and removes quickly, and the coupling accepts some movement. It has to match the groove system of the pipe, so state the pipe outside diameter (3″ is 88.9 mm, 4″ is 114.3 mm) and groove type. In a flanged plant, a DEMCO wafer or lug valve avoids adding flange adaptors.

categories.intro: Ring joint gaskets are solid metal rings that seal high-pressure flanges by being crushed into matching grooves cut in each flange face, used on API 6A wellhead equipment and ASME B16.5 flanges in high-pressure and high-temperature service. Indus supplies them from Dubai by ring number: Style R oval and octagonal rings from R-12 to R-66 for ASME Class 150 to 2500 and API 6B flanges, pressure-energised RX rings from RX-24 to RX-74, and BX rings from BX-151 to BX-169 for API 6BX flanges, with the flanges each ring fits listed on its page.

guidance.heading: Ring number, profile, then material
guidance.body: Take the ring number from the flange: the ASME size and class, or the API bore and pressure, or the number stamped on the old ring, which shares its groove number with the flange. Then the profile: R oval or octagonal, RX for API 6B flanges where pressure energising is wanted, or BX for 6BX flanges. Then material, which must be softer than the groove: soft iron, low-carbon steel, F5, 304, 316 or Inconel 625, set by the fluid, temperature and flange material. Send ring number, profile, material, quantity and any certificate needs.

standards.heading: ASME B16.20 and API 6A
standards.body: ASME B16.20 gives dimensions, tolerances, materials and marking for R, RX and BX ring joint gaskets used with ASME B16.5 and API 6A flanges; API 6A specifies the R, RX and BX rings for API flanges. B16.20 sets maximum hardness by material: soft iron 90 HB, low-carbon steel 120 HB, F5 130 HB, and 304, 316 and 347 stainless 160 HB. Rings are marked with the maker's identification, ring number and material. BX rings carry a pressure-passage hole to equalise pressure across the ring.

faq.q: Oval or octagonal R ring — which should I use?
faq.a: Use an octagonal ring in modern flat-bottomed grooves, and an oval ring where the groove may be the older round-bottomed type. An oval ring seals in either groove; an octagonal ring seals only in the flat-bottomed groove that current ASME B16.5 and API 6A flanges have, and is generally preferred there because its flat flanks give a more efficient seal. Both carry the same ring number for the same groove. If the flange is old or its groove profile unknown, check the groove before ordering octagonal.

faq.q: What do the material marks on a ring gasket mean, and how hard should it be?
faq.a: The mark identifies the material, and the ring must be softer than the flange groove so it deforms instead of the groove. Common marks are D for soft iron, S for low-carbon steel, F5 for 4–6% chrome steel and S304 or S316 for stainless; ASME B16.20 limits hardness to 90 HB for soft iron, 120 HB for low-carbon steel, 130 HB for F5 and 160 HB for 304 and 316. Pick the ring material to suit the fluid and temperature and to be softer than the flange, which is why stainless rings go in stainless or clad grooves.

faq.q: Why does a BX ring have a small hole drilled through it?
faq.a: The hole is a pressure-passage hole. A BX ring seals on both its inner and outer faces against the groove, and the hole lets pressure trapped in the groove on either side of the sealing contact equalise, so the ring is not forced out of its seat or locked under pressure. Every BX ring has one. Do not plug the hole, and do not substitute an R or RX ring in a 6BX flange: the BX groove and ring are a different family, and 6BX flanges make up face to face around a BX ring only.

faq.q: Why does the same R ring fit both an ASME flange and an API flange?
faq.a: Because the ring number is set by the groove, and API 6B flanges use the same R-series grooves as ASME B16.5 flanges. R-24, for example, fits 2″ Class 900 and 1500 flanges and API 2-1/16″ 3K and 5K flanges. Sharing a ring does not make the flanges interchangeable: bolt circle, bolt size and pressure rating can differ between the ASME and API flange, so check both flanges before joining them. Each ring's page lists the ASME and API flanges it fits.

faq.q: How do I identify an unmarked ring joint gasket?
faq.a: Measure it and match it to the ring tables. Record the profile (oval, octagonal, RX or BX), the pitch diameter through the centre of the ring section, the width, and the height. The pitch diameter and width identify the ring number, and the profile and height separate R from RX, since an RX ring of the same number is taller and has a different, asymmetric section. Better still, measure the flange groove, which does not wear like a used ring, or read the flange size and class or API bore and pressure stamped on the flange.

faq.q: How should a ring joint flange be made up?
faq.a: Clean and inspect both grooves, fit a new ring dry or lightly oiled, and tighten the bolts evenly in a cross pattern in several passes to the specified torque. Look for radial scratches, dents or corrosion in the groove sealing faces: a damaged groove will not seal however hard the bolts are pulled. Do not use tape, sealant or a soft gasket with the ring. API 6B flanges keep a small gap between the faces when made up; 6BX flanges close face to face. Retorque per your procedure after a thermal or pressure cycle if required.

categories.intro: Oilfield gate valves are full-bore isolation valves in which a flat gate slides across the flow path to seal against seats, used on wellheads, Christmas trees, frac manifolds and drilling mud systems. Indus supplies them from Dubai as authorised representative of Cameron, FMC, WOM and Stream-Flo, and in its own range: API 6A manual, slab and hydraulic fail-close gate valves from 1-13/16″ to 5-1/8″ at 5,000, 10,000 and 15,000 psi, in PSL 2 to PSL 3G, material classes EE and HH, and 7,500 psi mud gate valves.

guidance.heading: Bore and pressure, then service, then operation
guidance.body: Start with the API 6A nominal bore and rated working pressure, which fix the end flange and ring. Then the service: material class (EE for most sour wells, HH for severe H2S and CO2), temperature class, PSL and performance requirement, as your operator specifies. Then the operation: manual, or hydraulic fail-close where the valve must shut the well automatically, with the control pressure available. Mud gate valves for rig mud systems are chosen by size, 7,500 psi rating and end connection. Send bore, pressure, full API 6A designation, end connections and operator.

standards.heading: API 6A ratings and test pressures
standards.body: API 6A sets rated working pressures of 2,000, 3,000, 5,000, 10,000, 15,000 and 20,000 psi. Every valve body is shell tested hydrostatically at twice rated working pressure for ratings up to 5,000 psi and at 1.5 times for 10,000 psi and above. PSL 3G adds a gas test to PSL 3. PR2 requires performance verification testing of the design, and PR2F refers to the verification procedure of API 6A Annex F. Sour-service material classes meet NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156, which limits carbon and low-alloy steel to 22 HRC.

faq.q: Slab gate or expanding gate valve — what is the difference?
faq.a: A slab gate is a single solid gate that floats between two seats and seals when line pressure pushes it against the downstream seat. An expanding gate is a two-piece gate with angled faces that wedge apart at the end of travel, pressing mechanically against both seats, so it seals upstream and downstream even at low pressure. Slab gates are simpler, with fewer parts and a straight-through bore, and are widely used on wellheads and frac trees; expanding gates suit duty where a positive mechanical seal on both sides is wanted.

faq.q: What does FLS mean on a manual gate valve, and how does a fail-close hydraulic valve differ?
faq.a: On a Cameron valve, FLS is the name of the valve model, a forged-body slab gate valve, not an operating mode. A manual gate valve stays where its handwheel leaves it. A hydraulic fail-close gate valve has an actuator whose hydraulic pressure holds the gate open against a spring; when the pressure is lost or vented, the spring closes the valve, which is how a surface safety valve shuts a well in. Specify the actuator's control pressure available and whether a manual override or lock-open cap is needed.

faq.q: What do PSL 3G and PR2F mean on a gate valve?
faq.a: PSL 3G is product specification level 3 with an additional gas test: as well as the PSL 3 hydrostatic tests, the assembled valve is tested with gas, which finds leaks that water can miss, so it is specified for gas wells and high-pressure gas service. PR2F means the design has passed performance verification to API 6A Annex F, the PR2 test programme of pressure and temperature cycles and repeated operations under load. Both are design and test levels the buyer specifies; they are stated in each product title.

faq.q: Why are there 3-1/8″ and 3-1/16″ gate valves?
faq.a: They are the same nominal 3″ bore in the two API 6A flange families. 3-1/8″ is the 6B size for 2,000, 3,000 and 5,000 psi, with an R or RX ring; 3-1/16″ is the 6BX size for 10,000 psi and above, with a BX ring. A 3-1/8″ 5,000 psi valve will not bolt to a 3-1/16″ 10,000 psi flange. Give both the bore and the pressure rating when ordering a valve or a replacement, and check the ring number on the existing flanges.

faq.q: What is a mud gate valve and how is it different from an API 6A wellhead gate valve?
faq.a: A mud gate valve isolates drilling fluid in a rig's standpipe manifold, mud pump discharge and mud lines. It is built to tolerate abrasive mud and to be serviced on the rig, often with replaceable elastomer-bonded seats, and its 7,500 psi rating is a maker's rating rather than one of the API 6A rated working pressures. Ends are typically butt-weld, threaded or hammer union. Parts are model-specific: DEMCO DM 2000–5000 and DM 7500 valves look alike but share no seats, gates or kits.

faq.q: What does HH Inconel 625 cladded mean on a slab gate valve?
faq.a: HH is the most severe API 6A material class, for wells with high H2S and CO2, and requires corrosion-resistant alloy on all wetted surfaces. Cladding means a weld overlay of Inconel 625 applied to the bore, seal pockets and other wetted areas of a low-alloy-steel body, which gives the corrosion resistance of the alloy without making the whole body from it. The gate, seats and stem are corrosion-resistant alloy too. Use HH where the well's H2S and CO2 partial pressures and chlorides call for it.

categories.intro: Hammer unions are three-piece wing-nut connections, a male sub, a female sub and a lugged nut, that join flow iron and pipework quickly by striking the nut lugs with a hammer, used on frac, cementing, choke and kill, well test and mud lines. Indus supplies its own hammer unions from Dubai from Figure 50 at 500 psi to Figure 2002 at 20,000 psi, with threaded or butt-weld ends in standard and sour gas service, plus Figure 1003 misaligning, Figure 211 insulated and Figure 2202 sour 15,000 psi unions and Figure 207 blanking caps.

guidance.heading: Figure, size, service, then ends
guidance.body: Match the figure to the mating half already in the line; it sets the pressure rating, the nut thread and the seal. Then the nominal size, checking the size table, since some figures are reduced in larger sizes. Then the service: sour gas parts for any fluid with H2S, noting that a sour union can carry a lower rating than the standard union of the same figure. Then the end on each sub: line-pipe thread or butt weld to the pipe schedule. Send figure, size, service, end type and wall schedule for weld ends, and quantity of complete unions or halves.

faq.q: Why is a sour gas Figure 1502 union rated 10,000 psi when the standard one is 15,000 psi?
faq.a: Because sour service materials are softer. To resist sulphide stress cracking, NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 limits carbon and low-alloy steel to 22 HRC, and the lower-strength steel in the same Figure 1502 dimensions carries a lower rating, 10,000 psi on this shelf. The same applies to Figures 1002 and 1004, listed at 7,500 psi in sour service. For 15,000 psi in sour gas, use a union designed for it, such as Figure 2202. Always read the rating stamped on the union, not the figure number alone.

faq.q: What parts make up a hammer union, and can I order them separately?
faq.a: A hammer union has a male sub, which carries the wing nut, a female sub with the external thread the nut screws onto, and, in figures such as 1502, a replaceable elastomer seal ring seated in the female sub; some designs also use retainer segments to hold the nut. Halves, nuts and seal rings can be supplied separately, but only to the same figure, size and service as the half they mate with. Quote the figure, size, service and end type of the existing part.

faq.q: Threaded or butt-weld ends — which should I choose?
faq.a: Butt-weld ends for permanent pipework and the highest pressures, threaded ends for lighter duty and where welding is not practical. A butt-weld union must match the pipe's outside diameter and wall schedule and be welded to a qualified procedure, with hardness control and any post-weld heat treatment the sour service requires. Threaded ends screw onto line pipe threads and can be fitted without welding, but the thread can limit the joint's rating below that of the union. Check the rating for the end type on each product page.

faq.q: What is a Figure 1003 misaligning hammer union used for?
faq.a: It joins two lines that do not meet exactly in line. The Figure 1003 has a spherical seat between its subs so the connection seals with a small angle between them, which helps when rigging up temporary lines, manifolds and well test spreads where perfect alignment is hard to achieve. It is still a fixed connection, not a swivel joint, so it does not allow movement under pressure. It comes in standard and sour gas service; check the misalignment angle and rating on the product page.

faq.q: What is a Figure 211 insulated hammer union for?
faq.a: It breaks electrical continuity between two sections of pipe while joining them mechanically. Insulating components between the subs and nut stop current flowing through the joint, which isolates cathodically protected pipework from unprotected equipment and limits galvanic corrosion between dissimilar metals. It is rated 2,000 psi, so it suits low-pressure flow lines and utilities rather than high-pressure treating iron. Test the isolation with a meter after installation.

faq.q: How should a hammer union be made up and broken out safely?
faq.a: Check the figure, size and service stamped on both halves, clean the threads and seat, inspect the seal ring, align the subs, run the nut up by hand, then strike the lugs until the nut is fully home. Never strike a union, or try to tighten or loosen one, while the line is under pressure: bleed the line to zero first. Use a brass or other non-sparking hammer where a hazardous atmosphere is possible, and replace a union whose lugs are mushroomed, cracked or whose threads are worn.
